title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: this page continues the 'Longue Marche' discussion of the Fermat-type tower U_n -> U_1. Here U_1 is the projective line minus three points, realised as the line x_0+x_1+x_inf=0 inside G_m^3/G_m, and U_n is its pull-back under the n-th power map, i.e. the open Fermat curve of degree n. On the previous page Grothendieck takes the rational point s_{1/2}=(-1/2,-1/2,1). This is the point lambda=1/2, the fixed point of the involution lambda -> 1-lambda. He identifies the fibre of U_n at s_{1/2} with T_n(-1/2) x T_n(-1/2), where T_n(xi) is the mu_n-torsor of n-th roots of xi (normalise x_inf=1). In the limit, U_inf(s_{1/2}) = T_inf(-1/2) x T_inf(-1/2), a torsor under Zhat(1)^2.

This page draws the consequence. The Galois action (329) of Pi_Q = Gal(Qbar/Q) on this fibre (affine automorphisms) factors through Gal(Qtilde[(-1/2)^{1/inf}]/Q), where Qtilde = Q(mu_inf) is the universal cyclotomic extension. Because both factors are the same torsor, the action lands in a 'diagonal' affine group Zhat^* . Zhat(1), a semidirect product, which he seems to call N_Q^xi.

To measure the 'size' of the image he announces a general digression on Galois groups over Q of the multi-Kummer extensions Qtilde[xi_1^{1/inf}, ..., xi_N^{1/inf}]. The next page carries this out. Take a homomorphism A -> G_m(S), with A = Z and 1 |-> -1/2. Pull back the Kummer sequences 1 -> mu_n -> G_m -> G_m -> 1 to get extensions E_n(xi) of A_S by mu_n. In the limit this gives E_inf(xi), an extension of A_S by T(G_m). The resulting monodromy representation is pi_1(S) -> Aut(E_inf(xi)_sbar). This is standard Kummer theory over a base, in the language of extensions of etale group schemes.
errors: No substantive error on this page.
Previous page, second line of (332): 'x_0 = -1/2' should read x_inf = 1 (normalisation in G_m^3/G_m). It is either a slip or a transcription error.

Not stated here, but relevant to the announced 'size' question: since -1 is a root of unity, Qtilde[(-1/2)^{1/inf}] = Q(mu_inf, 2^{1/inf}). Since sqrt(2) lies in Q(mu_8), the image of Pi_Q in Zhat^* x| Zhat(1) is a proper subgroup of index 2, not the whole group. Presumably the digression is meant to detect exactly this kind of entanglement.

ideas.what: Galois action on the fibre of the (abelian/Fermat) tower over P^1-{0,1,inf} at the rational point lambda=1/2 is given by Kummer characters of -1/2 (equivalently 2) together with the cyclotomic character.
ideas.modern_name: Kummer cocycles / Galois action on fibre functors at rational base points of the Fermat tower (abelianised Galois action on pi_1 of P^1 minus 3 points)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ihara (Fermat tower, Jacobi sums, 1980s); Anderson; Deligne (1989); later Nakamura and Wojtkowiak for paths to rational points
ideas.where_published: Not in Esquisse or the published Longue Marche to my knowledge; unsure

ideas.what: Kummer theory over a base S: from a homomorphism A -> G_m(S), pull back the Kummer tower to get extensions 1 -> mu_n -> E_n(xi) -> A_S -> 1, the limit extension E_inf(xi), and the monodromy pi_1(S) -> Aut(E_inf(xi)).
ideas.modern_name: Kummer extensions / 1-motive [Z -> G_m] and its l-adic (Tate module) realisation
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical Kummer theory; 1-motives due to Deligne (Hodge III, 1974)
ideas.where_published: Similar formalism in SGA 7 (Grothendieck, biextensions) and SGA 4; unsure

ideas.what: Size of the image of Gal(Qbar/Q) in Zhat^* x| Hom(A, Zhat(1)) for multi-Kummer extensions Q(mu_inf, xi_i^{1/inf}).
ideas.modern_name: Open image of Kummer representations; entanglement of Kummer and cyclotomic extensions
ideas.usually_credited_to: Bashmakov, Ribet (1979); Schinzel; Lenstra, Moree, Stevenhagen (entanglement)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a standard reduction of the Galois action on a rational fibre of the Fermat tower to Kummer theory of -1/2 over Q(mu_inf). It is pedagogically nice and uses the symmetric point 1/2, but the content is classical and well covered by the later literature on Kummer images and the Ihara–Anderson Fermat-tower theory.
